Assessment incorporating literature:
- With inflation below target and market-based inflation compensation low, easing the policy rate is consistent with New Keynesian guidance to close output and inflation gaps without jeopardizing credibility (Woodford, 2003; Galí & Gertler, 1999). Stable survey-based expectations reduce the risk of unmoored inflation.
- The cited weakness in business fixed investment and exports is a meaningful drag on growth. Investment is both interest-sensitive and strongly linked to internal funds and financing conditions; ensuring ample reserves via T-bill purchases and repo operations should ease funding frictions and support inventory/capex (Kashyap, Lamont, and Stein, 1994; “Monetary Policy Effects transmitted through interest rate”).
- Empirical evidence indicates monetary policy shocks affect real activity (Sims, 1992), so the rate cut and liquidity operations are growth-supportive. Still, trade-related/global uncertainties temper the outlook.

Net tone: slightly positive—policy is accommodative against below-target inflation and investment softness, but persistent external headwinds keep optimism modest.
